method: WebSearch result summaries only (no page-level verification of each number unless noted); generic technical queries, no repo/host/client data sent. Nothing was installed or benchmarked on the VPS; every resourceFit is an estimate, NOT_MEASURED.

signals.title: intfloat/multilingual-e5-small: small multilingual embedding (384-d, 12 layers), MIT
signals.claim: MIT-licensed multilingual embedder; tech report gives 57.9 average on English MTEB (56 datasets); 384-d embeddings, 12 layers; safetensors ~471 MB. Multilingual MTEB average for the small variant not found in this run.

evidence.publisher: arXiv (Wang et al., Multilingual E5 Text Embeddings: A Technical Report)

signals.measuredOrClaimed: MEASURED_BY_AUTHORS (benchmark in tech report; not reproduced by ODG)
signals.resourceFit: Very good for 8 vCPU AVX2 / 22 GiB: ~118M params class (param count NOT confirmed in sources), <0.5 GB RAM in fp32; CPU throughput NOT_MEASURED.
signals.relevanceToODG: Cheapest FR/EN baseline embedder for client-document RAG; MIT avoids license gating. Requires 'query: '/'passage: ' prefixes.
signals.risks: Older (2024) and weaker than newer sub-1B models; 512-token context limits chunk size; param count unverified.

signals.title: EmbeddingGemma (~300-308M): top sub-500M on MMTEB, but Gemma license (not OSI)
signals.claim: Paper reports EmbeddingGemma ranks 8th overall on MTEB(Multilingual, v2), 17 places above the next sub-500M model; lead persists at 128-d Matryoshka truncation and 4-bit quantization. Mirror model cards list mean(task) 61.15 @768d, 58.23 @128d, Q4_0 60.62 (mirror figures NOT confirmed against official card).

evidence.publisher: Hugging Face (third-party mirror of model card)

signals.license: Gemma Terms of Use (gated, custom, NOT OSI open source)
signals.resourceFit: Good: ~300M params, <1.5 GB RAM fp32, smaller quantized; CPU latency NOT_MEASURED.
signals.relevanceToODG: Best quality-per-size multilingual candidate for FR/EN on CPU, if Gemma terms are acceptable for client work.
signals.risks: License requires owner/legal review (use restrictions, redistribution terms); gated download.

signals.title: Qwen3-Embedding-0.6B: 100+ languages, 32K context, up to 1024-d
signals.claim: Qwen3 Embedding series: 8B ranks #1 on MTEB multilingual (70.58, as of 2025-06-05). For 0.6B a third-party catalog lists MMTEB mean(task) 64.33 / mean(type) 56.00 (NOT confirmed against official card). 28 layers, 32K context, 100+ languages.
signals.license: Apache-2.0 per HF metadata (search summary flagged a wording conflict on the blog; verify on official card)
signals.resourceFit: Acceptable: 0.6B params, ~1.2 GB bf16 / less quantized (GGUF exists); slower than E-01/E-02 on CPU; NOT_MEASURED.
signals.relevanceToODG: Strongest permissive-licensed candidate; long context helps contracts/tenders; also code-capable.
signals.risks: Higher CPU cost per chunk; license wording to confirm; 0.6B score secondhand.

signals.title: nomic-embed-text-v2-moe: Apache-2.0 multilingual MoE, available in Ollama library
signals.claim: 475M total / 305M active params, 8 experts top-2, max 512 tokens, Matryoshka 768->256; ~100 languages per Ollama page (HF metadata lists only en/es - conflict); Apache-2.0; requires 'search_query:'/'search_document:' prefixes.
signals.measuredOrClaimed: CLAIMED (specs); MTEB scores not collected in this run
signals.resourceFit: Good; runs through the Ollama already on the VPS (ollama pull = network egress, owner-gated); NOT_MEASURED.
signals.relevanceToODG: Lowest-integration-cost path: reuse existing Ollama loopback endpoint (/api/embed) instead of adding a new runtime.
signals.risks: 512-token limit; language-coverage metadata conflict; pull requires egress.

signals.title: BAAI/bge-m3: dense + sparse + multi-vector in one model, MIT, 8192 tokens
signals.claim: Single model doing dense, sparse (lexical weights) and multi-vector (ColBERT-style) retrieval; 100+ languages; inputs up to 8192 tokens; dense dim 1024. Sparse/multi-vector outputs need FlagEmbedding (most libraries only support dense). 568M param figure NOT confirmed in this run.
signals.resourceFit: Heavier (XLM-R large class); feasible on 22 GiB but slowest of the candidates; NOT_MEASURED.
signals.relevanceToODG: Native hybrid (sparse+dense) for long FR legal/tender documents.
signals.risks: CPU cost; sparse mode needs Python FlagEmbedding (new dependency vs Node stack).

signals.title: sqlite-vec (asg017): dependency-free C SQLite vector extension, pre-v1, new ANN indexes in alpha
signals.claim: Pure C, no dependencies, MIT/Apache-2.0 dual license; vec0 virtual tables for float/int8/binary vectors; npm/pip/Go/Rust packages; README says pre-v1 with breaking changes expected; v0.1.10-alpha series adds ANN indexes (rescore, DiskANN; IVF experimental, not enabled). Default otherwise brute-force KNN.

evidence.date: release dates not confirmed in search

signals.resourceFit: Excellent: in-process, single file per DB, tiny footprint; brute force adequate up to ~1e5-1e6 vectors (estimate, NOT_MEASURED).
signals.relevanceToODG: Fits 'one SQLite file per tenant' isolation and reuse of an existing SQLite-based memory; combines with FTS5 for hybrid.
signals.risks: Pre-v1 API instability; ANN indexes alpha only; must pin version.

signals.title: Official SQLite 'vec1' ANN extension in development at sqlite.org
signals.claim: sqlite.org hosts vec1, an ANN vector search extension using SQLite's virtual-table interface; roadmap says no further features required before first release but 'Testing is insufficient'. Forum post by Dan Kennedy dated 2026-03-30.
signals.license: Presumed public domain like SQLite - UNVERIFIED
signals.resourceFit: Same in-process profile as sqlite-vec.
signals.relevanceToODG: Watch item: a first-party SQLite ANN would reduce third-party risk vs sqlite-vec.
signals.risks: Not released; self-declared insufficient testing; do not adopt yet.

signals.title: LanceDB (@lancedb/lancedb): embedded Apache-2.0 vector DB with Node bindings
signals.claim: Embedded (no server) columnar vector DB, Apache-2.0; current Node package @lancedb/lancedb (old 'vectordb' deprecated); data on local disk, sharable with Python; not supported on musl Linux or Windows ARM64.
signals.resourceFit: Good on glibc x86_64; larger native binary (Rust) than sqlite-vec; NOT_MEASURED.
signals.relevanceToODG: Option if corpus outgrows brute-force SQLite; built-in ANN + FTS.
signals.risks: Second storage engine beside existing SQLite memory (violates 'no parallel memory' unless it replaces); fast-moving API.

signals.title: vectorlite: hnswlib-backed SQLite extension (HNSW inside SQLite)
signals.claim: Authors claim vector queries significantly faster than sqlite-vec/sqlite-vss (HNSW); same README notes its brute-force mode is slower than sqlite-vec for 128-d.
signals.resourceFit: In-process; HNSW index RAM overhead; NOT_MEASURED.
signals.relevanceToODG: Fallback if ANN-in-SQLite needed before sqlite-vec ANN stabilises.
signals.risks: Smaller project, maintenance status unverified; vendor-style benchmark claims.

signals.title: Hybrid retrieval in SQLite: FTS5 BM25 + sqlite-vec KNN fused with Reciprocal Rank Fusion
signals.claim: Documented pattern: run FTS5 (BM25) and sqlite-vec KNN separately and fuse by rank: score = sum 1/(k+rank), k commonly 60, because BM25 and cosine scores are on incompatible scales. Full SQL example published; arXiv 'scrydb' paper evaluates rank fusion in SQLite on IR benchmarks.

evidence.type: academic paper - not read in full

signals.resourceFit: Excellent: zero extra services.
signals.relevanceToODG: Exact-term recall (SIRET, article numbers, product refs, French legal terms) that pure vectors miss; one SQLite file.
signals.risks: FTS5 tokenizer config for French (accents/diacritics: unicode61 remove_diacritics) must be chosen; query sanitisation needed for FTS5 syntax injection.

signals.title: Code-aware retrieval: tree-sitter symbol extraction + PageRank repo map (aider)
signals.claim: Aider builds a repo map with tree-sitter tag queries (defs/refs), a file-dependency graph ranked with PageRank (personalised to chat context), then emits the top-ranked symbols within a token budget; replaced its earlier ctags approach. Several Apache-2.0 reimplementations exist.
signals.measuredOrClaimed: CLAIMED (design description; no retrieval-quality benchmark collected)
signals.resourceFit: Excellent: CPU-only parsing, no model needed.
signals.relevanceToODG: ODG already has a change-impact graph / dependency graph: rank symbols over that existing graph rather than building a second one; use AST-based chunking (function/class boundaries) for code embeddings.
signals.risks: Duplication risk with existing ODG graph components; tree-sitter native bindings for Node add a build dependency.

signals.title: bubblewrap: unprivileged namespace sandbox; --unshare-all / --unshare-net / --die-with-parent / --new-session / stacked seccomp
signals.claim: --unshare-all unshares user, IPC, PID, network, UTS, cgroup (user/cgroup as try); --share-net re-enables net; --new-session calls setsid (else block TIOCSTI via seccomp); --die-with-parent uses PR_SET_PDEATHSIG; --seccomp FD loads cBPF, newer versions add --add-seccomp-fd to stack filters.
signals.measuredOrClaimed: DOCUMENTED (man page); ODG has prior PROVEN bwrap launchSpec (internal, not re-verified here)
signals.license: LGPL-2.0-or-later (from general knowledge - UNVERIFIED in this run)
signals.resourceFit: Near-zero overhead; already installed (0.11).
signals.relevanceToODG: Keep as primary sandbox; --unshare-net gives a network namespace with only loopback = hard no-egress for client-doc jobs. NOTE: a fresh netns has its own loopback, so the host Ollama at 127.0.0.1:11434 is NOT reachable from inside; needs a bind-mounted Unix socket proxy or running inference outside the sandbox.
signals.risks: Shares host kernel (namespace escape = kernel bug class); isolation strength depends on the seccomp profile ODG supplies.

signals.title: Ubuntu AppArmor restriction on unprivileged user namespaces (affects bwrap/podman/nsjail)
signals.claim: Ubuntu (since 23.10/24.04) restricts unprivileged userns creation via kernel.apparmor_restrict_unprivileged_userns; binaries need an AppArmor profile granting 'userns' (bwrap-userns-restrict profile shipped in apparmor package on newer releases). Disabling via sysctl is system-wide and discouraged.
signals.resourceFit: n/a
signals.relevanceToODG: Since bwrap already works on the VPS, a profile is presumably in place; adding nsjail/podman/runsc --rootless would each need an AppArmor userns profile = root (owner-gated).
signals.risks: Any new sandbox binary may fail silently-ish ('Userns create restricted'); do not flip the sysctl.

signals.title: Landlock LSM: unprivileged filesystem + TCP (ABI>=4) + UDP (ABI>=10, dev docs) restrictions
signals.claim: Unprivileged processes can restrict themselves; TCP bind/connect rules per port since ABI v4; UDP rights appear in v7.2-rc docs at ABI v10; ABI discovered via landlock_create_ruleset(NULL,0,LANDLOCK_CREATE_RULESET_VERSION) with best-effort degradation.
signals.measuredOrClaimed: DOCUMENTED; whether Landlock is enabled in the VPS kernel's LSM list NOT_OBSERVED
signals.resourceFit: Negligible overhead.
signals.relevanceToODG: Defence-in-depth inside bwrap: deny-all TCP connect except allowlisted ports, restrict writes to tenant dir. Can be applied from a tiny helper or via existing tooling.
signals.risks: Port-based only (no IP/host allowlist); UDP control only on very new kernels; must check 'landlock' is in active LSMs.

signals.title: gVisor (runsc): user-space kernel; systrap platform needs no KVM; --rootless mainly for 'runsc do'
signals.claim: Systrap (default platform) intercepts syscalls with signals + shared memory, needs no /dev/kvm; KVM platform requires KVM. Rootless: runsc --rootless maps caller to root in a new userns, 'create' unsupported, mainly suitable for 'runsc do'. Combination rootless+systrap not explicitly confirmed by docs.
signals.measuredOrClaimed: DOCUMENTED; overhead NOT_MEASURED on this host
signals.resourceFit: Works on a KVM guest without nested virt (systrap); syscall-heavy workloads pay overhead (amount NOT_MEASURED); installing binary + Docker runtime registration = root.
signals.relevanceToODG: Strongest isolation achievable WITHOUT nested virt: separate kernel surface for untrusted client-doc parsers (PDF/Office).
signals.risks: Install/AppArmor profile owner-gated; compatibility gaps for some syscalls; rootless mode limited.

signals.title: Firecracker microVMs require /dev/kvm; not usable on a KVM guest without nested virtualization; jailer needs root
signals.claim: Firecracker requires the KVM module and rw on /dev/kvm; not well tested under nested virt; without nested virt there is no /dev/kvm. The jailer handles privileged setup (cgroups, chroot/pivot_root, device node ownership) then drops privileges - setup requires elevated permissions.
signals.measuredOrClaimed: DOCUMENTED; presence of /dev/kvm on VPS NOT_OBSERVED (V178 P0 inventory reported no GPU; nested-virt status not stated)
signals.resourceFit: Likely NOT available (needs nested virt from hosting provider).
signals.relevanceToODG: Reject for now; revisit only if provider enables nested virt or bare metal.
signals.risks: Wasted effort if pursued without /dev/kvm.

signals.title: nsjail (Google): namespaces + Kafel seccomp-bpf + cgroups v1/v2 + rlimits
signals.claim: Supports UTS/MOUNT/PID/IPC/NET/USER/CGROUP/TIME namespaces, chroot/pivot_root, RO mounts, Kafel syscall policy DSL, rlimits and cgroups v1/v2 for CPU/memory/pids. Explicit rootless mode not confirmed in search results (user-namespace UID maps supported).
signals.resourceFit: Low overhead; would need build/install + AppArmor userns profile.
signals.relevanceToODG: Only marginal gain over bwrap (built-in rlimits/cgroups/seccomp DSL); prefer extending existing bwrap launchSpec + systemd-run --user scope for limits (no 2nd sandbox).
signals.risks: Parallel sandbox component (anti-duplication); cgroup delegation requires systemd user setup.

signals.title: Rootless Podman: pasta default since 5.0, requires /etc/subuid + /etc/subgid entries
signals.claim: Rootless networking via pasta (default since Podman 5.0) or slirp4netns; each user needs subuid/subgid ranges, else commands fail; run 'podman system migrate' after changes. Ubuntu resolute (26.04) ships podman 5.7.0.
signals.resourceFit: Moderate overhead (images, storage); package install + subuid edit = root once.
signals.relevanceToODG: Docker CLI present but rootful Docker daemon membership = root-equivalent; rootless Podman with --network=none is the container option that keeps no-root operation after setup.
signals.risks: Docker group access is root-equivalent (general knowledge, not sourced here); --network=none semantics under rootless not confirmed in this run.

signals.title: Ollama: binds 127.0.0.1:11434 by default, local prompts not seen by Ollama; cloud features disable flag; keep_alive controls model/KV residency
signals.claim: FAQ: local runs - 'We don't see your prompts or data'; OLLAMA_HOST changes bind (default loopback); OLLAMA_KEEP_ALIVE / API keep_alive (0 = unload immediately after response); OLLAMA_NO_CLOUD=1 disables cloud features; OLLAMA_NOHISTORY disables readline history (CLI only). Linux logs via journalctl; OLLAMA_DEBUG=1 more detail. No official statement found on whether debug logs contain prompt text.
signals.resourceFit: Already installed.
signals.relevanceToODG: Set OLLAMA_NO_CLOUD=1 and keep loopback bind; use keep_alive=0 for client-document jobs so model state/KV cache is not kept between tenants; never run with OLLAMA_DEBUG on client data. Changing the system service env = root/systemd (owner-gated).
signals.risks: Vendor privacy claim is not a measurement - must be enforced by egress control (G-02); 'ollama pull' needs egress; model registry contains cloud models.

signals.title: No-egress enforcement for LLM processing: network namespace (bwrap --unshare-net) + Landlock TCP connect deny
signals.claim: A process in a new network namespace has no route off-host (only its own loopback) - bwrap --unshare-net / --unshare-all; Landlock ABI>=4 can additionally deny TCP connect to all but allowlisted ports, unprivileged. Host-level nftables owner-filtering (skuid) would need root.
signals.measuredOrClaimed: DOCUMENTED mechanism; ODG enforcement NOT re-measured in this run
signals.resourceFit: Zero cost.
signals.relevanceToODG: Client-doc pipeline = parser + embedder + retrieval inside --unshare-net (no network at all); inference reached via a bind-mounted Unix socket to a loopback-only Ollama proxy. Proof = negative test (connect to public IP fails) as evidence.
signals.risks: The Ollama daemon itself runs outside the sandbox and retains host network; it must be constrained separately (systemd IPAddressDeny etc. = root).

signals.title: fscrypt: per-directory encryption; only 'fscrypt setup' (global) always needs root; filesystem needs encrypt feature
signals.claim: fscrypt tool: 'fscrypt setup' (creates /etc/fscrypt.conf) is the only step that always requires root; kernel API usable by unprivileged users, but non-root users cannot securely remove keys; filesystem must have the encrypt feature flag (ext4: tune2fs -O encrypt - from general knowledge, UNVERIFIED in this run).
signals.resourceFit: Low overhead (AES-NI on Haswell).
signals.relevanceToODG: Per-tenant directory keys = crypto-isolation of client data at rest; good fit once owner enables FS feature + setup.
signals.risks: Enabling ext4 encrypt feature on the root FS is a root, low-reversibility operation (owner-gated); metadata (file sizes/timestamps) not hidden.

signals.title: SQLCipher Community (BSD-style, AES-256) vs better-sqlite3-multiple-ciphers (MIT, SQLite3MultipleCiphers)
signals.claim: SQLCipher Community Edition: BSD-style license usable in closed-source with attribution, 256-bit AES full-DB encryption; 5.0.0-beta moves default to AES-256-GCM (beta). better-sqlite3-multiple-ciphers is a Node fork of better-sqlite3 using SQLite3MultipleCiphers (default cipher sqleet/ChaCha20), MIT; SQLCipher-compatible mode exists but not verified here.
signals.resourceFit: Low overhead; in-process.
signals.relevanceToODG: Per-tenant encrypted SQLite file (vectors + FTS + chunks) with a per-tenant key - root-free encryption at rest. Must verify sqlite-vec extension loads into the cipher build.
signals.risks: Key management is the real problem (where the key lives); extension-loading compatibility with sqlite-vec unverified; switching SQLite driver touches existing memory component.

signals.title: age (age-encryption.org/v1): simple file encryption, X25519/scrypt recipients, post-quantum hybrid in recent versions
signals.claim: Spec defines X25519 recipients (ephemeral ECDH, HKDF-SHA-256, ChaCha20-Poly1305 wrap of 128-bit file key) and scrypt passphrase recipients; Go library recommends supporting only X25519 for new systems; recent versions add mlkem768x25519 post-quantum recipients; interoperable Rust impl (rage).
signals.license: BSD-3-Clause (from general knowledge - UNVERIFIED in this run)
signals.resourceFit: Trivial.
signals.relevanceToODG: Root-free encryption for client document blobs, backups and evidence bundles, one recipient key per tenant.
signals.risks: Files must be decrypted to tmpfs/RAM for processing - plaintext hygiene still required; key custody.

signals.title: EU AI Act amended by Digital Omnibus on AI - Regulation (EU) 2026/1744 in force 2026-07-27; high-risk Annex III deferred to 2027-12-02
signals.claim: Omnibus signed 2026-07-08, published OJ 2026-07-24, in force 2026-07-27 (law-firm reports). Stand-alone (Annex III) high-risk obligations move from 2026-08-02 to 2027-12-02; high-risk safety components of regulated products to 2028-08-02. Adds CSAM / non-consensual intimate content prohibitions; SME relief extended to 'small mid-caps'. The broader Digital Omnibus (incl. GDPR changes) is still in the legislative process.
signals.measuredOrClaimed: LEGAL_FACT per secondary sources - official EUR-Lex text of Reg. 2026/1744 NOT fetched (UNVERIFIED against primary source)
signals.resourceFit: n/a
signals.relevanceToODG: Updates ODG memory anchor 'AI-Act Art.113 2027-12-02' - consistent with the omnibus deferral; verify on EUR-Lex before citing to clients.
signals.risks: Relying on law-firm summaries; exact article wording and transitional rules must be read from the OJ.

signals.title: GDPR anchors: Art. 5(1)(c) data minimisation, Art. 25 data protection by design/default, Art. 32 security of processing
signals.claim: Art. 5(1)(c): data adequate, relevant and limited to what is necessary. Art. 25: implement principles effectively, taking account of state of the art (pseudonymisation cited as example). EDPB Guidelines 4/2019: effectiveness is at the heart of DPbD. Art. 32 encryption wording NOT retrieved in this run (general knowledge: Art. 32(1)(a) lists pseudonymisation and encryption) - UNVERIFIED.
signals.resourceFit: n/a
signals.relevanceToODG: Justifies: local-only processing, chunk/log minimisation, per-tenant encryption, retention limits on embeddings/caches (embeddings of personal data are personal data - interpretation, not sourced here).
signals.risks: Interpretations (embeddings = personal data, logs) need DPO/legal confirmation; not legal advice.

recommendations.embedding: Shortlist for a local CPU bake-off (ODG must measure FR/EN retrieval on its own non-client corpus before choosing; all scores above are author/secondary claims): (1) nomic-embed-text-v2-moe via the EXISTING Ollama endpoint (Apache-2.0, lowest integration cost); (2) Qwen3-Embedding-0.6B (Apache-2.0, 32K ctx, strongest permissive; heavier); (3) multilingual-e5-small (MIT) as fast baseline. EmbeddingGemma only after owner/legal review of Gemma terms. bge-m3 only if native sparse is needed and a Python dep is accepted. Model download = egress = owner-gated.
recommendations.vectorStore: Reuse existing SQLite memory: sqlite-vec (pinned version, brute-force KNN) + FTS5 BM25 fused with RRF (k=60) in ONE SQLite file per tenant. No second store. Watch sqlite.org vec1; escalate to sqlite-vec DiskANN / LanceDB only if measured latency at real corpus size requires it.
recommendations.sandbox: Keep bubblewrap as the sole sandbox (--unshare-all, --die-with-parent, --new-session, seccomp) + Landlock FS/TCP rules as defence-in-depth + systemd-run --user scopes for CPU/memory limits. gVisor systrap is the only stronger option viable without nested virt (owner-gated install). Firecracker rejected (needs /dev/kvm). nsjail/Podman add a parallel component for marginal gain.
recommendations.egressControl: Client-document jobs run with no network namespace connectivity (bwrap --unshare-net); inference reached only via a bind-mounted Unix socket to loopback Ollama; Landlock deny TCP connect; Ollama with OLLAMA_NO_CLOUD=1, loopback bind, keep_alive=0 for tenant jobs; host-level egress deny for the ollama service (systemd IPAddressDeny / nftables) = root, owner-gated. Evidence = automated negative egress test per run.
recommendations.encryption: Root-free now: per-tenant SQLCipher/SQLite3MultipleCiphers DB file + age-encrypted document blobs, plaintext only on tmpfs inside the sandbox. Owner-gated later: fscrypt per-tenant directories (needs FS encrypt feature + 'fscrypt setup' as root) or LUKS volume (root). VPS has NO swap (good: no plaintext/KV pages swapped to disk) - keep it that way or use encrypted swap.

Does sqlite-vec load as an extension into SQLCipher / SQLite3MultipleCiphers builds used from Node 22?

Do Ollama server logs (non-debug) ever contain prompt text? No official statement found.
Primary-source (EUR-Lex) verification of Regulation (EU) 2026/1744 dates and GDPR Art. 32 wording.
Where do per-tenant keys live (owner-held, TPM absent on VPS?) - key custody design is the main open risk.
